## PDF page 213

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=213)

```text
                           CHAPTER SEVENTEEN



                              4BETTING


A 4bet is the second re-raise preflop and a crucial part of contending as
players get more aggressive before the flop. As more players are making
3betting a staple in their preflop strategy, well-timed 4bets allow you to fight
for pots with monsters and bluff hands alike.

The average player 4bets infrequently, to the point where their 4betting range
is comprised of KK+, or maybe QQ+/AK. But with some technical exploration
you will find it easier to identify spots where your opponent is 3betting a bit
too much and continuing a bit too infrequently – allowing you to ramp up the
aggression with a variety of hands you may otherwise fold.

These exercises will guide you through 4betting spots in the same way the
3betting chapter looked at 3bets. This means you are looking at different
continuance ranges, different sizes, and how the SPR is impacted if your 4bet
gets called.

The times your 4bet faces a 5bet, which is often an all-in, will be explored in
upcoming chapters.

TOOLS TO USE: Any range software (Flopzilla, Equilab, PokerCruncher, etc.)
and a calculator will work.




                                   PA G E 2 1 3
```

## PDF page 214

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=214)

```text
                    P O K E R M AT H & P R E F L O P WO R K B O O K


PROCESS: Each page contains a single 4bet scenario. Read the prompt and
then begin by filling in the %-form for your opponent’s 3bet range and the
two possible continuance ranges.

Then fill out the table below for each 4bet size. Jot down both your oppo-
nent’s folding frequency and what the SPR would be if your opponent just
called your 4bet.

TAKEAWAYS: Pay careful attention to the continuance ranges. Even when
your opponent’s 3betting range is less than 10%, you can still find auto-profit
4bets if they only continue with nutted hands.

While the specifics will impact the BE% of your 4bet size, it is common to have
a BE% around 60% when you 4bet to 20bb. Put a star next to any spots where
your opponent folds more than 70% of the time or less than 33% of the time.

GLGL.




                                     PA G E 2 1 4
```
